title: Shipped tor 0.4.9.11 misses security release 0.4.9.12
location: flake.lock (nixpkgs pin); fix belongs in pkgs/overrides.nix
description: tor 0.4.9.12 was published 2026-09-08, one day after the pin and one day before the audited commit. Upstream: 'another security release containing several high security fixes... We very strongly recommend upgrading as soon as possible.' Client-relevant fixes: hostile directory cache marking relay descriptors unusable (TROVE-2026-034), consensus-diff memory DoS class (TROVE-2026-042), OOM use-after-free (TROVE-2026-043). tor carries all node traffic and terminates five inbound onion services on the recommended deployment.
evidence: Deployed closure evaluates to tor 0.4.9.11; dist.torproject.org lists 0.4.9.12; gitlab ReleaseNotes for 0.4.9.12 confirm the security content and date 2026-09-08.
impact: DoS and descriptor-poisoning exposure on the node's most-exposed daemon, requiring a malicious relay/cache position in the consensus. Anonymity degradation and availability loss are the realistic outcomes; RCE less so for a client-only node.
why_the_scan_missed_it: tor advisories are tracked as TROVE IDs, not NVD CVEs, so the weekly vulnix scan is structurally blind to them.
recommendation: Add a version-guarded override pinning tor 0.4.9.12 in pkgs/overrides.nix (the fork's stated policy for exactly this case). Add tor-announce to the subscription list in docs/security-audit-2026-08-14.md section 5, which currently lists no tor feed.
file: flake.lock (nixpkgs pin); fix belongs in pkgs/overrides.nix

title: btcpayserver 2.4.3 lags security release 2.4.4
description: BTCPay Server 2.4.4 (2026-09-07) is a security-focused update strengthening permissions and validation around invoices, API keys, server administration and other sensitive operations; upstream recommends all server administrators update. The fork's override was written for 2.4.3 (the previous security release) and pins exactly that, so the recommended deployment runs an internet-facing payment processor one security release behind.
evidence: Deployed closure evaluates to btcpayserver 2.4.3; GitHub latest release is 2.4.4 published 2026-09-07T13:28:37Z; blog.btcpayserver.org/btcpay-server-2-4-4/ is titled 'BTCPay Server 2.4.4: Security Update'.
impact: Application-layer permission and validation weaknesses in the web app reachable through the btcpayserver onion service. The in-the-wild /lnd-rest/btc/v1/changepassword attack from the same post does NOT apply to this fork: lnd REST is never reverse-proxied publicly here and the lnd wallet uses a per-node random password with startup auto-unlock.
why_the_scan_missed_it: BTCPay advisories carry no CVEs, so vulnix cannot see them; the version-guarded override mechanism is the fork's intended channel but was not re-run against this release.
recommendation: Bump the override to 2.4.4 with a regenerated nuget lockfile (procedure documented in pkgs/btcpayserver/default.nix). Fold 'check upstream release feed on every pin update' into the weekly routine for btcpayserver and nbxplorer.

title: wireguard preset exposes lnd admin REST on 0.0.0.0 but never asserts the firewall is enabled
category: missing guard on a load-bearing assumption
location: modules/presets/wireguard.nix:97-101 (only assertion is netns incompatibility), :148-180 (firewall extraCommands), :192 (restAddress = "0.0.0.0")
description: When lndconnect is enabled, the preset sets services.lnd.restAddress = "0.0.0.0" and relies entirely on the NixOS firewall (default-drop plus a scoped accept rule) for protection. The preset never asserts networking.firewall.enable. In the pinned nixpkgs, the entire firewall module config including extraCommands and allowedUDPPorts is gated behind mkIf cfg.enable, so with networking.firewall.enable = false anywhere in the user's config (VMs, containers, upstream-firewall setups) the macaroon-admin REST API listens on every interface with no filtering, and the preset evaluates cleanly.
evidence: nixpkgs firewall.nix line 321: 'config = lib.mkIf cfg.enable'; wireguard.nix contains no firewall assertion; the code comment at line 182 states the port is 'guarded by the firewall' as an assumption.
impact: Full admin REST API exposure (macaroon-authenticated endpoints, plus wallet-setup endpoints during the pre-unlock window) on all interfaces in misconfigured-but-plausible deployments. Compounds the tracked-and-deferred 0.0.0.0 bind in docs/wireguard-rest-bind.md.
recommendation: Add an assertion that networking.firewall.enable is true whenever the wg lndconnect mode is active (or whenever restAddress would be 0.0.0.0). This is independent of, and much cheaper than, the deferred rebind work in docs/wireguard-rest-bind.md.
file: modules/presets/wireguard.nix:97-101 (only assertion is netns incompatibility), :148-180 (firewall extraCommands), :192 (restAddress = "0.0.0.0")

title: wireguard preset has no release-gating CI coverage
location: .github/workflows/test.yml (matrix: default, regtest, netns); test/ci/test-info.nix (derives scenario list from that matrix); test/run-tests.sh:302 (wireguard-lndconnect only in local buildable list)
description: The firewall fixes in the audited commit itself (restrictPeer insert-at-top, interface-pinned REST accept) are only exercised by the wireguard-lndconnect scenario, which is not in the CI matrix that gates the release branch. The commit message cites a green local VM suite, but the release ruleset only requires the CI checks.
impact: A future commit can regress the wireguard firewall rules and still advance the release branch with all checks green.
recommendation: Add wireguard-lndconnect to the test.yml scenario matrix (it is a two-node VM test, modest cost), or fold a wg assertion into the default scenario.
file: .github/workflows/test.yml (matrix: default, regtest, netns); test/ci/test-info.nix (derives scenario list from that matrix); test/run-tests.sh:302 (wireguard-lndconnect only in local buildable list)

title: Dead code: fetchNodeModules build support kept after RTL removal
location: pkgs/build-support/fetch-node-modules.nix; referenced only by its own wiring at pkgs/default.nix:16
description: The node_modules fetcher was needed by the removed RTL packaging. Nothing in modules, packages, or tests consumes it anymore; the flake already removes it from exported packages.
impact: Build-time-only surface and repo bloat; no runtime exposure.
recommendation: Delete the file and its callPackage entry, per the fork's own delete-over-add policy.
file: pkgs/build-support/fetch-node-modules.nix; referenced only by its own wiring at pkgs/default.nix:16
